strategy.bottleneck: [compute/mainloop-bound composite] The cuDNN fp32 NCHW conv2d pair dominates: 2×77.3 GFLOP (16.8M outputs × 2304 MACs) ⇒ ≥1.48 ms even at the 104.8 TFLOPS FP32/TF32 peak, while every profiled custom kernel (stats 45.9 µs, apply 114.5/73.3 µs) totals only ~284 µs and already runs at 88–98 % of DRAM SOL, i.e. zero internal headroom.
strategy.primary_optimisation_method: Layout switch to channels_last (NHWC) for the kept cuDNN mainloop, so cuDNN dispatches its NHWC TF32 tensor-core implicit-GEMM conv kernels instead of the NCHW FFMA/transpose path. Mainloop stays vendor-library (allowed); only memory format changes. The GN/SiLU/residual kernels are pure elementwise+reduction and are re-indexed for NHWC (warp covers contiguous C), keeping their traffic identical and fully coalesced. One extra 134 MB transpose of x is amortized because the residual then reuses the NHWC copy.
strategy.modification_plan:
1) forward() exact code actions: replace `x_c = x.contiguous()` with `x_c = x.contiguous(memory_format=torch.channels_last)`; replace `w1 = conv1_weight.contiguous()` / `w2 = ...` with `.contiguous(memory_format=torch.channels_last)`. Both F.conv2d calls then emit channels_last outputs automatically (drop the `out.contiguous()` calls; use `out.contiguous(memory_format=torch.channels_last)` only if `not out.is_contiguous(memory_format=torch.channels_last)`).
2) Add at module import: `torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = True` and keep `torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 = True` (shapes are fixed: 8×256×64×128, 3×3, pad 1 ⇒ autotune cost amortized, matches reference TF32 numerics).
3) Re-index gn_stats_partial_kernel for NHWC (no shared-memory tiling; smem stays at the existing 32-float warp-reduction scratch, ~256 B/block, far below the 99 KB/block limit): grid = (pixel_chunks, N); block = 256 threads where thread t owns channel t of a pixel row (row = 256 contiguous floats = 1 KB, perfectly coalesced). Each thread grid-strides over pixels of its chunk accumulating v and v*v for its single channel; then reduce across the 8 lanes of each group with `__shfl_down_sync` at offsets 4,2,1 (lane&7==0 holds the group partial), and write 32 group partials per (n, chunk) to `partial[(n*32+g)*chunks + chunk]` (deterministic, no atomics).
4) gn_finalize_kernel: one block of 256 threads per (n,g) pair or grid=NG, block=128; sum `chunks` partials, compute mean = S/65536, rstd = rsqrt(max(Q/65536 - mean*mean,0)+eps). Keep the same 2-stage split (avoids atomics, preserves fp32 accuracy).
5) Re-index gn_silu_apply_kernel<VEC,RESID> for NHWC: linear index over N*H*W*C with float4 vectorization; channels are 8-per-group and float4 is 4-aligned, so a float4 never straddles a group ⇒ compute `g = ((idx4*4) % 256) >> 3`, load mean/rstd for that group and gamma/beta as float4 from a per-channel precomputed pair of tensors. Precompute per-(n,c) `scale = gamma[c]*rstd[n,g]`, `bias = beta[c] - mean[n,g]*scale` in the finalize kernel into two (N,256) float arrays, then the apply kernel is one FMA + SiLU + optional residual add per element (no per-thread division/rebuild of scale).
6) Residual: pass the already-converted NHWC `x_c` as the residual tensor to gn_silu_add — no extra transpose.
7) Output: return the channels_last result directly (same logical shape/values; allclose is layout-agnostic). Only if the harness demands NCHW-contiguous, append `.contiguous()` behind a module flag.
8) Anti-regression autotune: on the first forward, time the NCHW path and the NHWC path with torch.cuda.Event (2 iterations each) and cache the winner in a module-level dict keyed by (shape, dtype); subsequent calls take the cached branch. This guarantees no slowdown if cuDNN's NCHW kernel is already optimal.
9) Validate atol ≤ 2.8e-3 vs reference (TF32 in both paths ⇒ same 10-bit mantissa class); do NOT switch to fp16/bf16 inputs (bf16 would inject ~0.1 absolute error into the 2304-term dot product).
strategy.evidence: Metrics: gn_silu_apply<1,1> moves 3×67.1 MB in 114.53 µs = 1758 GB/s ≈ 98 % of 1792 GB/s peak (dram_throughput 88.15 %); gn_stats_partial 89.8 % DRAM at 1567 GB/s. Root cause: all custom kernels are already at bandwidth SOL, so the only remaining large cost is the unprofiled cuDNN conv pair, 155 GFLOP ⇒ ≥1.48 ms at 104.8 TFLOPS, ~5× the entire 284 µs GN segment; NCHW fp32 conv forces cuDNN off its NHWC tensor-core implicit-GEMM kernels. Refutation of the alternative 'apply kernel is the bottleneck': its 94.55 % long-scoreboard stall is pure DRAM latency at 98 % of peak bandwidth with the minimum possible byte count (1 read + 1 residual read + 1 write), so no kernel-local change (more ILP, occupancy, vector width) can help.
strategy.expected_metric_change: Conv segment: kernel names change to NHWC TF32 tensor-core implicit-GEMM; conv sm__pipe_tensor / SM throughput ↑ (>60 %) and conv duration ↓ 25–50 %. New transpose pass adds ~134 MB (~75 µs) once, so end-to-end must still drop; GN kernels must keep gpu__dram_throughput ≥85 % and unchanged byte counts (l1tex sector counts per element must not rise — verify NHWC float4 accesses stay 32-B-sector perfect, l1tex__t_sector_hit_rate not worse than today's 7.4 %). Anti-regression: if the timed NHWC path is not ≥5 % faster end-to-end than NCHW, the autotune must fall back to NCHW; numerical max_atol must remain <2.8e-3.

strategy.bottleneck: [Tensor-core/compute-bound composite] The cuDNN 3x3 conv pair (2x77.3 GFLOP, >=1.48 ms even at 104.8 TFLOPS TF32) dominates the forward; all profiled GN kernels total only ~284 us and already run at 88-89% DRAM SOL (gn_silu_apply<1,1> 114.5 us = 1758 GB/s ~ 98% of 1792 GB/s), so no kernel-local headroom remains in fp32.
strategy.primary_optimisation_method: Mixed-precision downcast of the whole block to FP16 (channels_last) with FP32 accumulate: run both cuDNN convs on FP16 tensor cores (209.5 vs 104.8 TFLOPS => up to 2x on the dominant mainloop) and keep the intermediates half, which simultaneously halves every byte moved by the DRAM-SOL-bound GN stats/apply kernels. FP16 has the same 10-bit mantissa as the TF32 path the reference already uses (cudnn.allow_tf32 default True), and all values (|conv out| <~ 300) are far inside FP16 range.
strategy.modification_plan:
1) Precision/layout entry (do FIRST): in forward, build xh = x.contiguous(memory_format=torch.channels_last).to(torch.float16) and w1h/w2h = conv weights .to(torch.float16).contiguous(memory_format=torch.channels_last) (weights only 2.36 MB). Keep the original fp32 NCHW x tensor alive for the residual. Set torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=True once at module init.
2) Convs: out = F.conv2d(xh, w1h, None, 1, 1) and F.conv2d(h1, w2h, None, 1, 1) -> both dispatch to cuDNN FP16 NHWC implicit-GEMM tensor-core kernels with FP32 accumulate; conv output tensors are half NHWC (33.5 MB instead of 67.1 MB each).
3) Rewrite gn_stats_partial_kernel for half NHWC: contiguous dim is C=256, a group = 8 consecutive channels. Each thread loads one float4 (= 8 halves = exactly one group of one pixel), converts to float, accumulates sum/sumsq into a single group accumulator; lane i of a warp handles group i, so one warp covers all 32 groups of one pixel with a perfectly coalesced 512 B request. Grid = (splits, N); per-block reduce 32 group partials via shared float[32][2] across warps, write partial[(n*G+g)*splits+s]. Keep the existing gn_finalize_kernel (mean/rstd per (n,g)) unchanged.
4) Rewrite gn_silu_apply for pass 1 (half NHWC in -> half NHWC out): precompute per-channel scale=gamma[c]*rstd, bias=beta[c]-mean*scale into shared float[256] per block (mean/rstd chosen by c/8, so only n varies per block). Each thread reads one float4 (8 halves), converts to float, applies FMA scale/bias, SiLU, converts back to half, writes one float4. Fully vectorized 16 B/thread, no branch divergence.
5) Pass 2 kernel (half NHWC y + fp32 NCHW residual -> fp32 NCHW out): stage a tile of P=128 pixels x 256 channels of the normalized+SiLU result in shared memory as half. SHARED-MEM BUDGET: 128*256*2 B = 64 KB <= 99 KB per block limit on sm_120 (single buffer, no double buffering). Phase A: threads read y as float4 (coalesced NHWC), apply scale/bias/SiLU, store half into smem[p][c]. __syncthreads(). Phase B: remap threads so a warp covers 128 contiguous pixels of a single channel c: read residual x[(n*C+c)*HW + p0..] as float4 from fp32 NCHW (coalesced), add smem[p][c], write out fp32 NCHW as float4 (coalesced). Output is a plain contiguous NCHW fp32 tensor, identical layout to the reference.
6) Host launcher: template kernels on the half type; keep the split/partial-buffer sizing logic, but compute splits from N*G with the new (splits, N) grid. All allocations via torch::empty on y.options() (device preserved).
7) Numerics guard: run one offline validation over all workloads; require max_atol < 2.8e-3. If any workload fails, gate the fp16 path behind a module-level flag and fall back to the current fp32 channels_last path (keep the existing fp32 kernels compiled in the same extension). Also add a first-call timing autotune (fp16 vs fp32 path) and cache the winner, so a slower cuDNN fp16 engine cannot regress.
8) Do not touch get_inputs/get_init_inputs; do not move tensors across devices; no in-place writes (out is a fresh empty_like-shaped fp32 tensor, residual x is read-only).

Root cause: the block is split between a bandwidth-saturated fp32 GN segment (284 us, 469 MB) and a TF32 conv pair needing >=1.48 ms for 154.6 GFLOP at 104.8 TFLOPS; FP16 tensor cores double conv peak to 209.5 TFLOPS and halve GN bytes. Refutation of 'GN apply is the bottleneck': it is already at ~98% of achievable bandwidth with the minimum byte count, so occupancy/ILP/vector-width changes cannot help - only reducing bytes per element (fp16) can, which this method does.

(2) gn_stats_partial and gn_silu_apply: DRAM bytes halved -> durations ~45.7 us -> ~25 us and ~114.5 us -> ~62 us, while gpu__dram_throughput must stay >=85% (proving still bandwidth-saturated, not newly latency-bound). strategy.bottleneck: [compute/mainloop-bound] The unprofiled cuDNN fp32 NCHW 3x3 conv pair (2 x 77.3 GFLOP = 154.6 GFLOP) dominates: >=1.5 ms even at 104.8 TFLOPS, versus only ~232 us for all profiled GN kernels, which already run at 87-89% DRAM SOL. Default PyTorch cudnn.benchmark=False picks a heuristic direct/implicit-GEMM algo instead of the 2.25-4x-cheaper Winograd F(2x2/4x4,3x3) algorithm for this fixed shape.
strategy.primary_optimisation_method: Convolution algorithm selection: drive both convs through cuDNN with an exhaustive, shape-cached algorithm search (cudnnFindConvolutionForwardAlgorithmEx) so the Winograd-nonfused path is chosen for 3x3/stride1/pad1, C=256. This is a provable algebraic work reduction (9 multiplies per 3x3 output tile -> 4 for F(2x2,3x3)), directly attacking the compute-bound mainloop; it is mechanism-distinct from prior layout (NHWC) and precision (FP16) attempts, which changed data format, not the arithmetic algorithm.
strategy.modification_plan:
Checklist (items 1-2 are the exact core rewrite):
1. ModelNew.__init__: add `torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = True`, `torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 = True`, `torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = True`. This alone forces PyTorch's conv dispatcher to run exhaustive algo search per (shape,dtype) and cache it, replacing the heuristic algo with the fastest (expected WINOGRAD_NONFUSED for 3x3 s1 p1 C=256).
2. Add to the load_inline extension (extra_ldflags=["-lcudnn"], `#include <cudnn.h>`, `#include <ATen/cudnn/Handle.h>`) a function `conv3x3(x, w)`:
   - `auto handle = at::native::getCudnnHandle();`
   - build `cudnnTensorDescriptor_t` xDesc/yDesc as NCHW FLOAT (N=8,C=256,H,W), `cudnnFilterDescriptor_t` wDesc (256,256,3,3, NCHW), `cudnnConvolutionDescriptor_t` convDesc with pad=1,1 stride=1,1 dil=1,1 CUDNN_CROSS_CORRELATION, CUDNN_DATA_FLOAT; set `cudnnSetConvolutionMathType(convDesc, CUDNN_TENSOR_OP_MATH_ALLOW_CONVERSION)`.
   - Static `std::unordered_map<key,(algo,ws_bytes)>` keyed by (N,C,H,W). On first call for a key: allocate a 256 MB byte workspace tensor and call `cudnnFindConvolutionForwardAlgorithmEx(handle,...,requestedAlgoCount=8, returnedAlgoCount, perfResults, ws_ptr, ws_bytes)`; pick the first perfResult with `status==CUDNN_STATUS_SUCCESS` and `memory<=ws_limit`; store algo+memory in the map.
   - Every call: get/grow a static cached workspace tensor to the cached size, then `cudnnConvolutionForward(handle, &one, xDesc, x, wDesc, w, convDesc, algo, ws, ws_bytes, &zero, yDesc, y)` into `torch::empty({N,C,H,W}, x.options())`.
3. Replace both `F.conv2d(..., padding=1)` calls in forward with `self.ext.conv3x3(x_c, w1)` and `self.ext.conv3x3(out, w2)`; keep all tensors contiguous NCHW fp32 so the existing GN kernels are untouched.
4. Guard: wrap the extension conv in try/except (Python) and a C++ fallback to `at::conv2d` if find returns no usable algo or descriptor creation fails, so correctness never depends on cuDNN algo availability.
5. Accuracy guard: after the one-time search, if the selected algo is a WINOGRAD variant, run one validation call comparing against `at::conv2d` on the first invocation (max abs diff); if diff > 1.0e-3 on conv output, blacklist WINOGRAD algos for that key and re-pick the next fastest (IMPLICIT_PRECOMP_GEMM). Store the decision in the same static map so the check runs once, not per forward.
6. Do NOT touch gn_stats_partial / gn_finalize / gn_silu_apply: they are at 87-89% of DRAM peak with minimal byte counts; any change there is wasted effort.
7. Ensure the algorithm search and workspace allocation happen outside the timed steady state by keying the cache on shape (harness warmup call performs the search once).
8. Keep output allocation on the input device (`x.options()`), no host syncs in forward except the existing `eps` scalar handling (hoist: only call `.item()` if eps is a Tensor).
9. Validate end-to-end max_atol < 2.8e-3 across workloads; if the cuDNN-direct path is not faster than `F.conv2d` with benchmark=True, keep step 1 only (it already enables the same exhaustive selection with zero risk).

strategy.bottleneck: [Composite: compute-bound cuDNN 3x3 conv pair serialized with bandwidth-bound GroupNorm kernels]. Hottest non-removable segment: conv1/conv2 (154.6 GFLOP, >=1.4 ms at 104.8 TFLOPS, ~6% DRAM use) followed strictly in-order by gn_stats_partial (47.7 us, 88.2% DRAM, 5.9% SM) and gn_silu_apply (114.6 us, 87.7% DRAM, 14.0% SM). Each phase idles the resource the other saturates; no kernel-local headroom remains.
strategy.primary_optimisation_method: Multi-stream batch-chunk software pipelining: split the batch (samples are fully independent for conv, GroupNorm groups and residual) into chunks and run them on 2-3 CUDA streams so a chunk's DRAM-saturated GN kernels (88% DRAM, <15% SM) execute concurrently with another chunk's compute-bound cuDNN conv (high SM, ~6% DRAM). Complementary resource profiles make the ~230-285 us GN segment nearly free, and smaller per-chunk working sets add L2 reuse. Requires switching extension launches to getCurrentCUDAStream().
strategy.modification_plan:
1) CRITICAL correctness/enabling edit in the CUDA host launcher: replace `at::cuda::getDefaultCUDAStream()` with `at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream()` in gn_silu_impl so all three kernels (stats, finalize, apply) execute on the stream active in Python; otherwise pipelining silently serializes on the default stream.
2) Add an out-parameter variant so chunk results can be written into a slice of one pre-allocated output: `gn_silu_add_out(y, residual, gamma, beta, out, num_groups, eps)` (and `gn_silu_out`) that TORCH_CHECKs out.is_contiguous() && out.sizes()==y.sizes() and passes out.data_ptr<float>() instead of calling torch::empty_like. Keep existing entry points as thin wrappers.
3) Python side, ModelNew.__init__: create a static list of side streams `self.streams = [torch.cuda.Stream() for _ in range(2)]` (lazily, on first forward, on x.device) plus reusable `torch.cuda.Event()` objects. Do not create streams per call.
4) forward(): keep cudnn.benchmark=True / the winning conv config from history unchanged (not the counted method). Allocate `out = torch.empty_like(x_c)` once.
5) Chunking: `nchunk` chosen from B: chunk_size = max(1, B // 4) so B=8 -> 4 chunks of 2 samples (still 4.2M conv outputs/chunk => ample parallelism for 170 SMs). Slices `x_c[i0:i1]` are contiguous views; no copies.
6) Ordering in: record `ev_in` on the current stream after computing x_c/w1/w2; each side stream calls `s.wait_event(ev_in)`.
7) Per chunk c (assigned round-robin to stream s = streams[c % len]): inside `with torch.cuda.stream(s):` do (a) t = F.conv2d(x_c[i0:i1], w1, padding=1); (b) t = ext.gn_silu(t, g1, b1, 32, eps); (c) t = F.conv2d(t, w2, padding=1); (d) ext.gn_silu_add_out(t, x_c[i0:i1], g2, b2, out[i0:i1], 32, eps). Because consecutive chunks alternate streams, chunk c's memory-bound GN kernels overlap chunk c+1's conv.
8) Allocator safety: call `t.record_stream(s)` is unnecessary (t created and consumed on s), but call `x_c.record_stream(s)` and `out.record_stream(s)` for every side stream so the caching allocator does not reuse those blocks before the side streams finish.
9) Ordering out: after the loop, each side stream records `ev_out[i]`; the current stream `torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_event(ev_out[i])` for all i; return out.
10) One-time autotune (static dict keyed by shape): time nchunk in {1 (single-stream baseline), 2, 4} and #streams in {2,3} over a few iterations with torch.cuda.synchronize; cache the winner; if no configuration beats the single-stream path by >=3%, permanently fall back to nchunk=1 single stream (anti-regression).
11) Do not change any kernel body math, vector width, block sizes, or the conv algorithm; the only mechanism introduced is stream-level overlap, so numerics stay bit-identical per chunk (GN groups are per-sample, so chunking cannot change results).
12) Validate max_atol < 2.8e-3 against the reference on the largest workload before enabling the pipelined path.

strategy.bottleneck: [DRAM-bandwidth-bound, redundant-traffic] The GroupNorm segment: gn_silu_apply<1,1> 114.5 us and gn_stats_partial 46.4 us both run at ~88% DRAM SOL (1.5-1.76 TB/s) with l1tex/L2 hit rates ~0.4-7%. The stats kernel streams the whole 67.1 MB conv output, then the apply kernel re-reads the identical 67.1 MB from DRAM (L2 hit 0.62% => zero inter-kernel reuse), so one full tensor read per GroupNorm is pure waste.
strategy.primary_optimisation_method: Persistent cooperative single-pass GroupNorm: one kernel keeps each group's slice resident in registers, computes sum/sumsq, does a grid.sync(), then applies scale/bias+SiLU(+residual) from those registers. Metrics show both GN kernels are DRAM-saturated (88% dram_throughput, 79-92% long-scoreboard stalls, 91% achieved occupancy), so no occupancy/ILP tuning can help; only removing the redundant 67.1 MB re-read (x2 GNs = 134 MB, ~75-95 us) reduces time. Also deletes 2 stats + 2 finalize launches.
strategy.modification_plan:
1) EXACT REWRITE (traffic elimination): replace the 3-kernel sequence (gn_stats_partial -> gn_finalize -> gn_silu_apply) with ONE cooperative kernel `gn_fused_persistent<RESID>`. Each thread loads its slice ONCE into registers: `float4 reg[8];` (8 float4 = 32 regs of data, 256 threads => 8192 floats = 32 KB per block). Phase A accumulates sum/sumsq from reg[] (no second load). Phase B, after `grid.sync()`, recomputes `a = gamma[c]*rstd`, `b = beta[c] - mean*a` and writes `silu(a*reg[i].x+b)` (+residual) with float4 stores. Net effect: GN1 traffic 192->128 MiB, GN2 256->192 MiB.
2) EXACT INDEXING/LAUNCH: fixed shapes N=8,C=256,G=32,cpg=8,HW=8192 => group_size=65536 floats; K = 65536/8192 = 8 blocks per group. Launch with cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel, grid = min(K*NG, maxActiveBlocksPerSM(from cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor)*170) rounded DOWN to a multiple of K; persistent loop over rounds: `for (round = 0; round < nRounds; ++round) { g = (blockIdx.x/K) + round*groupsPerRound; if (g < NG) {...} grid.sync(); }` — keep the loop trip count identical for all blocks so grid.sync() is uniform (no deadlock).
3) Reduction plumbing: allocate `acc[groupsPerRound*2]` in global (or use a persistent `float2* acc` of size NG*2). Phase A: warp-shuffle reduce -> one `atomicAdd(&acc[gLocal].x/.y, ...)` per block (only 8 atomics per group per round; privatized, negligible). Zero acc for the NEXT round inside phase B after use, then a second `grid.sync()` before the next round to avoid RAW/WAR on acc.
4) Stats->params: after the first grid.sync(), every block reads `acc[gLocal]` (broadcast, L2 hit), computes `mean = s*inv_n`, `rstd = rsqrtf(fmaxf(q*inv_n - mean*mean,0)+eps)` in registers — this removes the separate 2.24 us gn_finalize launch and its uncoalesced 33%-excessive-sector accesses.
5) Channel index from element offset: `long long base = (long long)g*65536 + (blockIdx.x%K)*8192;` element linear index `e = base + i*1024 + threadIdx.x*4` (float4 units scaled); `c = (int)((e/8192) & 255)`; since a block spans exactly one channel (8192 floats = 1 channel), hoist `c` and (a,b) OUT of the inner loop as scalars — zero per-element divides.
6) Register budget check: 8 float4 (32) + addressing/reduction (~20) ~= 56 regs/thread => 64K/(56*256) = 4 blocks/SM = 32 warps/SM (67% occupancy) with 8 outstanding float4 loads per thread => ample MLP to keep DRAM >=85%.
7) Host side: keep F.conv2d (cuDNN) untouched; call `gn_fused(y, gamma, beta, nullptr)` after conv1 and `gn_fused(y, gamma, beta, &x_c)` after conv2. Query cooperative-launch support and max active blocks ONCE (static cache).
8) Fallback: if cooperative launch is unsupported, occupancy*SMs < K (cannot host one full group), or group_size%8192 != 0 (non-fixed shapes), dispatch the existing 3-kernel path unchanged.

strategy.primary_optimisation_method: L2 cache blocking: process the block in batch chunks whose live intermediate footprint fits the reported 18.87 MB L2 persisting window (one sample = 8 MB), reusing fixed buffers, and pin them with a cudaStreamSetAttribute accessPolicyWindow (hitProp=Persisting, missProp=Streaming). Conv output written by cuDNN then stays L2-resident for the stats pass and for the apply pass, converting two 67 MB DRAM reads per GroupNorm into L2 hits. Matches metrics: kernels are at ~98% of peak bandwidth, so only byte removal helps.
strategy.modification_plan:
1) (Traffic rewrite, must be item 1) Restructure ModelNew.forward into a batch-chunk loop: chunk size cs = max(1, floor(8 MiB / (C*H*W*4))) → cs=1 here (per-sample bytes = 256*64*128*4 = 8 MiB). For each chunk: xc = x_c.narrow(0, n0, cs); t1 = F.conv2d(xc, w1, padding=1); t2 = gn_silu(t1); t3 = F.conv2d(t2, w2, padding=1); gn_silu_add_out(t3, xc, → out.narrow(0,n0,cs)). All GN stats are per-(n,group) and both convs are spatial-only, so per-sample chunking is exactly equivalent (no cross-sample dependency).
2) (Residency rewrite) Add a host helper called once per process: cudaDeviceSetLimit(cudaLimitPersistingL2CacheSize, 16*1024*1024); then per forward set on the current stream a cudaStreamAttrValue accessPolicyWindow {base_ptr = t1.data_ptr(), num_bytes = min(chunk_bytes, 16 MiB), hitRatio = 1.0f, hitProp = cudaAccessPropertyPersisting, missProp = cudaAccessPropertyStreaming}; reset with cudaCtxResetPersistingL2Cache() after the loop. Because the caching allocator hands back the same block each iteration, the window address stays valid for all chunks; re-set the window whenever the observed pointer changes.
3) Expose the window setup as two extension entry points: set_l2_window(tensor, bytes) and reset_l2_window(); call set before the GN pair of each chunk, reset at end of forward.
4) Add an out-tensor variant gn_silu_add_into(y, residual, gamma, beta, out_slice, G, eps) so the final apply writes directly into the preallocated full output slice — no extra copy, no extra 67 MB write.
5) In gn_silu_apply_kernel add a template flag STREAM_OUT: when true (final residual-add store only, never re-read) use __stcs on the float4 store so the output does not evict the persisting input; keep normal stores for the GN1 output (it is re-read by conv2).
6) Retune launch geometry for the smaller chunk so the GPU stays full: in gn_silu_impl change the split heuristic to splits = clamp(4096 / NG, 1, 64) and keep the ≥4096-elements-per-block guard; for cs=1, NG=32 → splits=64 → 2048 stats blocks (~2 waves/SM). Apply-kernel grid becomes (HW/4/256, cs*C) = (8, 256) = 2048 blocks, still ≥2 waves/SM.
7) Allocate the two small stat tensors (partial, ms) once per forward outside the chunk loop (sized for one chunk) and pass raw pointers, to avoid 8× allocator churn.
8) Keep cuDNN conv (mainloop-keep) unchanged; only the launch granularity changes. Keep torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = True so the per-chunk shape is autotuned once.
9) No shared-memory tiling is introduced (SMEM gate N/A): per-block smem stays at the existing 1280 B for warp reductions, far below the 99 KB limit.
10) Guard/fallback: on the first call, time the chunked path vs the current single-shot path with CUDA events (once, cached in a module-level dict keyed by shape); if the chunked path is not ≥3% faster, permanently fall back to cs = B (current behaviour). If cudaDeviceSetLimit or the stream attribute call returns an error, silently continue without the window (chunking alone still yields natural L2 reuse).
11) Validate numerics: chunking is bitwise-identical for GN (per-sample stats) and for conv (per-sample independence); assert max_atol < 2.8e-3 versus reference in a one-off debug check.

strategy.bottleneck: [compute/tensor-core-bound composite] The unprofiled cuDNN fp32 3x3 conv pair (2x77.3 GFLOP = 154.6 GFLOP; >=1.48 ms even at the 104.8 TFLOPS TF32 peak) dominates, while every profiled custom kernel is already at DRAM SOL: gn_silu_apply<1,1> 113.7 us moving 3x67.1 MB = 1.77 TB/s (~99% of 1792 GB/s), gn_stats_partial 46.0 us at 89% DRAM. No kernel-local headroom remains in fp32.
strategy.primary_optimisation_method: Downcast the two convolutions to FP16 (channels_last, FP32 accumulate) so cuDNN dispatches NHWC tensor-core implicit-GEMM at 209.5 TFLOPS instead of 104.8 TFLOPS TF32, halving the dominant conv cost and simultaneously halving the bytes the DRAM-bound GN kernels must read. Round 2 nominally tried this but its speedup (1.1064) is numerically identical to round 1's pure channels_last result (1.1063), proving its perf-based fallback fired and the FP16 path was never exercised; this plan removes that fallback and eliminates cast/copy overhead.
strategy.modification_plan:
1) Precision rewrite (core): replace both F.conv2d calls with FP16 channels_last convs. At module import set torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=True. In forward, build x_h = x.to(torch.half).contiguous(memory_format=torch.channels_last) ONCE; cache w1_h/w2_h = weight.to(half).contiguous(channels_last) in a dict keyed by weight.data_ptr() so the cast runs only on the first call (weights are reused every iteration). out = F.conv2d(x_h, w1_h, None, 1, 1) -> half NHWC; cuDNN keeps FP32 accumulate (compute type float), matching the reference's TF32-level error budget (both have 11-bit effective mantissa).
2) Remove ALL performance-based fallbacks. Do NOT time fp32 vs fp16 and pick the winner (that is what neutralized round 2). Keep only a one-time correctness guard: on the first call compare the fused result against the fp32 path with atol 2.5e-3 and set a module flag; only on failure revert to fp32 channels_last for subsequent calls.
3) Rewrite gn_stats_partial for NHWC half input with channel-major thread mapping: index = ((n*H+h)*W+w)*C + c. Block = 256 threads, thread t owns channel c=t; grid = (splits, N). Each thread grid-strides over pixels p, loading __half2 pairs (two pixels of the same channel are NOT contiguous, so instead load a full 256-channel row per pixel: threads 0..255 read consecutive halves => 512 B fully-coalesced per pixel) and accumulates float sum/sumsq in registers for its own channel. Write per-(n, split, c) partials to a float buffer (N*splits*256*2 floats).
4) Rewrite gn_finalize: for each (n, g) sum the 8 channel partials over all splits, mean = S/(8*HW), rstd = rsqrt(S2/(8*HW) - mean^2 + eps). Group stats are exactly the sum of per-channel sums (channels in a group are contiguous in NHWC), so this is an exact rewrite.
5) Rewrite gn_silu_apply for NHWC half: load 256 float-scale/bias values (scale=gamma[c]*rstd[g(c)], bias=beta[c]-mean*scale) into shared memory once per block (1 KB); thread t handles channel c=t of a pixel, reads __half2/half8 vectors, computes a = __half2float(v)*scale+bias, a = a/(1+expf(-a)). GN1 variant writes half NHWC (feeds conv2); GN2 variant adds the fp32 residual and writes the final output.
6) Final-output layout: GN2's kernel stages a 32x32 (channel x pixel) half tile in shared memory (2 KB) so the fp32 NCHW store is coalesced along W; residual x is read in fp32 NCHW coalesced. This keeps the returned tensor bit-layout identical to the reference (contiguous NCHW) with no extra .contiguous() pass.
7) Keep FP32 for every reduction/normalization/residual arithmetic; only the conv inputs/outputs and the GN1 intermediate are half. Error budget: per-term relative error ~5e-4, conv output relative error ~7e-4, post-GN absolute error ~1e-3 < 2.8e-3 tolerance.
8) Byte accounting: casts add 67 MB read + 33 MB write (~56 us once per forward for x only, weights cached), while GN reads drop from 67 MB to 33.5 MB per pass (-100 MB) and conv time should drop ~600-700 us.
9) Guards: TORCH_CHECK C%32==0 and C==256 fast path; assert 16 B alignment for half8 loads; keep local-memory spills at 0.
